framework_catalog.scope: A curated publication reference catalog, not an exhaustive list of NIST publications or ISO standards.

items.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
items.summary: Organizes cybersecurity outcomes for governance and risk conversations across six functions, with profiles to describe current and desired outcomes.
items.applicability: A flexible reference for organizations that choose it; Harbor does not establish a regulatory obligation or assign implementation tiers.
items.scope: Selected subcategory identifiers for 12 starter topics; no complete profile or full CSF assessment is supplied.

items.name: NIST Risk Management Framework (SP 800-37)
items.summary: Connects system preparation, categorization, control work, authorization decisions, and monitoring through a managed lifecycle.
items.applicability: Use when the chosen system and governance context calls for RMF. A Harbor risk acceptance is not a federal authorization to operate.
items.scope: Reference guidance only; no RMF task catalog or authorization workflow mapping is included.

items.name: NIST SP 800-53 Security and Privacy Controls
items.summary: Provides selectable security and privacy controls to tailor to system boundaries, organizational needs, and risk decisions.
items.applicability: Selecting references does not establish a baseline, satisfy every control enhancement, or prove a control operates.
items.scope: Selected base control identifiers only; no complete catalog, parameters, enhancements, or normative requirements are distributed.

items.name: NIST SP 800-53A Control Assessment Procedures
items.summary: Supports planning and executing control assessments, including selection of assessment objects, methods, and sufficient examination depth.
items.applicability: Tailor a competent assessment to its scope and objectives; Harbor evidence approval alone does not execute the published procedures.
items.scope: Reference guidance only; no assessment-objective catalog or procedure completion tracking is supplied.

items.name: NIST SP 800-53B Control Baselines
items.summary: Describes security and privacy starting baselines and tailoring considerations. The 5.2.0 version update did not change its baselines.
items.applicability: Select and tailor a baseline through the applicable system categorization and governance process; the Harbor starter pack is not a baseline.
items.scope: Reference metadata only; no low, moderate, high, or privacy baseline is imported or asserted.

items.name: NIST SP 800-30 Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments
items.summary: Guides assessment of threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, consequences, and uncertainty as inputs to informed risk decisions.
items.applicability: The Harbor 1-5 scoring anchors are project choices, not a NIST-prescribed formula or calibrated probability model.
items.scope: Reference guidance only; no claim of completing all assessment activities.

items.name: NIST SP 800-161 Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
items.summary: Connects supplier and product risk to organizational strategy, acquisition, operating processes, and continuing oversight.
items.applicability: Adapt to the supplier service, dependencies, information flows, and decision authority. A questionnaire score alone is not supplier assurance.
items.scope: Reference guidance only; selected supplier themes also link to SP 800-53 controls, without claiming complete SP 800-161 coverage.

items.name: NIST SP 800-171 Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information
items.summary: Addresses confidentiality protection for controlled unclassified information in scoped nonfederal systems and organizations.
items.applicability: Relevant where the information and applicable contract or agreement establish a CUI requirement. Inclusion does not determine contractual applicability, a mandated revision, CMMC status, or legal compliance.
items.scope: Reference metadata only; no CUI requirement crosswalk, assessment, or compliance determination is supplied.

items.name: NIST SP 800-61 Incident Response and CSF Community Profile
items.summary: Connects incident preparation, coordinated response, recovery, and lessons learned with cybersecurity risk decisions using a CSF 2.0 community profile.
items.applicability: Use to structure the supplier incident exercise and incident-response improvement work. A tabletop is a simulation, not proof of actual response performance.
items.scope: Reference guidance only; no complete community profile or incident assessment is imported. Revision 3 supersedes Revision 2.

items.name: ISO/IEC 27001 Information Security Management Systems
items.summary: Sets requirements for an information security management system. The 2024 amendment addresses climate-related considerations in organizational context.
items.applicability: Use an authorized edition and applicable amendment for an ISMS scope, risk treatment, applicability decisions, and conformity assessment.
items.scope: Selected management-clause and Annex A identifiers with original project summaries; no licensed standard text or complete Annex A is reproduced.

items.name: ISO/IEC 27002 Information Security Controls
items.summary: Offers guidance for selecting and putting information security controls into practice. It supports an ISMS but is not itself a certification standard.
items.applicability: Consult an authorized copy to interpret selected controls in context; a shared identifier is not evidence of effective implementation.
items.scope: Selected control identifiers and original topic labels only; no full 93-control inventory, attributes, or guidance text is reproduced.

items.name: ISO/IEC 27005 Information Security Risk Management
items.summary: Offers guidance for information security risk assessment, treatment, communication, and review in support of management decisions.
items.applicability: Adapt a risk method to the organization and ISMS context; the Harbor score bands are not an ISO-mandated calculation.
items.scope: Reference guidance only; no licensed guidance text or claim of complete implementation.

limitations: Publication metadata and selected identifiers are informational references, not a compliance decision or certification.
Mappings are project-authored partial associations. They are not official NIST/ISO mappings, equivalence claims, or complete requirement coverage.
A local evidence-backed control count does not demonstrate every referenced requirement, an entire assessment period, or an effective management system.
ISO requirements and implementation guidance must be consulted in an authorized copy. No licensed standard text is bundled.
Reference-only publications intentionally have no selected control mappings in this pack; zero mapped controls is not an assessment result.
Sources were checked on the stated date. Revalidate editions, applicability, and source content before organizational adoption.

framework_mappings.scope: Project-authored partial links for the 12 fictional starter control topics. References are assessment prompts, not satisfaction claims or an official NIST/ISO crosswalk.
limitations: The pack omits most framework content. An unmapped requirement is a scoping gap, not a passed or failed control.
Selected topics can relate to several requirements while demonstrating only part of each. Assess scope, enhancements, parameters, period and evidence separately.
ISO identifiers and original topic labels are reference metadata. Validate interpretation against an authorized standard; no licensed requirement or implementation text is included.
The 2024 amendment to ISO/IEC 27001 is recorded in the publication catalog but is not assessed by these 12 mappings.
Coverage recognizes these exact reference strings only. Other valid references remain visible as unknown-to-pack entries until explicitly curated.

The exercise can expose planning gaps; complete response plans, resourcing and operational tests require separate review.
Contact and notice checks examine one supplier notification path; complete arrangements and actual execution require separate assessment.
A joint exercise tests selected preparation assumptions; organization-wide roles, plans and tools remain in scope.

Acceptance rationale should refer to an assessed scenario; this decision record alone does not complete a risk assessment.
Exception authority and expiry can support risk strategy execution; the organization-wide strategy and criteria require separate evidence.
Recorded assessment reasons relate to the risk method; complete criteria, repeatability and all in-scope risks require review.
A bounded acceptance documents one treatment decision; treatment selection, applicability records and full implementation remain separate.
Inventory reconciliation and retesting address selected vulnerability identification; the full asset population and other assessment methods need review.
Scanner reconciliation and retest support vulnerability monitoring; authenticated scope, tool coverage and assessment depth need validation.
Remediation and retest address selected flaws; update integrity, testing, deployment safeguards and systemic correction require additional assessment.
Tracked findings and retesting support vulnerability handling; discovery coverage, prioritization and preventive measures require broader evidence.

Recovery and emergency-access tests touch authenticator handling; issuance, storage, rotation and revocation require additional evidence.
Path and recovery samples support authentication assurance; all interfaces, authenticator handling and failure cases remain in scope.

framework_coverage.scope: Counts cover distinct local controls with exact reference strings recognized by the bundled partial mapping pack. Evidence-backed means effective status plus current approved evidence within the control's test cadence. Counts do not measure full-framework coverage, conformance, certification, or equivalence. An unknown reference is outside this curated pack, not necessarily invalid.
